title: vs.audio-stream
description: One effect-package sample stream (effect block 13): what its 64-byte AKAO header holds, beside the decoded channels (N.wav and N.sfz per channel) in the same directory, audio/streams/akao/<id> (Docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md §6.5, Content/AudioStreamJson.hpp). It is a record of the stream, not its source: the runtime reads the stream from its effect package and refuses one whose stream.json differs, so VS.Extract streams writes it again. audio/streams/index.json lists the packages and offsets that hold each id. The header is magic AKAO, +16 bytes per channel, +20 the loop, +24 the format flags, +28 the SPU pitch and +32 the start page; Sound_Cutscene_StartStream reads nothing else, and the rest is zero. The native reader also checks what a schema cannot: that loop_frame comes before frames and that sample_rate is the rate spu_pitch plays.

display_name.description: Optional informational name, not an identity or gameplay field.

id.description: FNV-1a 64 of the whole stream block, header included, in lowercase hexadecimal. It names this directory; the runtime finds the stream's files by it.

channels.description: Header +24 bit 0: 2 for a stereo stream, whose channels interleave in 2048-byte chunks.

frames.description: Samples per channel. Header +16 holds the bytes per channel: 16 bytes of ADPCM per 28 frames.

sample_rate.description: Hz: spu_pitch * 44100 / 4096, rounded to the nearest hertz. The rate of the WAV files beside this one.

spu_pitch.description: Header +28: the SPU voice pitch, where 4096 plays 44,100 frames a second. Every disc stream holds 2048 (22,050 Hz).

repeat.description: Header +24 bit 1: whether playback returns to loop_frame at the end.

loop_frame.description: The frame a repeating stream returns to; 0 when it does not repeat. Header +20 holds it as a byte offset into the interleaved channel data, so a stereo loop starts a whole 2048-byte chunk of each channel (a multiple of 3584 frames) and a mono loop a whole 28-frame block.

start_page.description: Header +32: the player stores it and never reads it. Every disc stream holds 2048.
